claims.title: Military coercion
claims.statement: Strikes alone rarely achieve maximal Iranian political compliance.
claims.geography: Iran; explicitly declared maximal objectives of each strike campaign
claims.effect: Compliance sustained for 180 days after a campaign
claims.falsifier: A documented maximal demand is fully met for 180 days without occupation.
claims.support: Survival and resistance after major damage
claims.alternative: Negotiations, sanctions, limited military objectives; do not treat delay as failure.
claims.attribution: Report-derived hypothesis; not a verified direct quotation from Pape.
claims.plain: Strikes alone seldom force Iran to meet its attackers' maximum political demands.

claims.title: Maritime denial
claims.geography: Strait of Hormuz; commercial oil passage
claims.effect: At least 10% lower volume than the prior four-quarter mean for 30 days, with corroborated Iranian interference
claims.falsifier: 90 days of normal passage under a documented credible threat and active countermeasures.
claims.alternative: Demand, voluntary rerouting, production cuts and tracking coverage can change flows.
claims.attribution: Report-derived hypothesis; not a verified direct quotation from Pape.

claims.title: Political concessions
claims.statement: Maritime coercion yields durable political concessions.
claims.effect: A substantive policy change sustained for 180 days with documentary attribution to maritime pressure
claims.falsifier: An agreed concession is reversed within 180 days, or a completed negotiation produces none.
claims.support: Documented policy reversal tied to coercion
claims.alternative: Routine diplomacy, unrelated bargains and temporary ceasefires are competing explanations.
claims.attribution: Report-derived hypothesis; not a verified direct quotation from Pape.

claims.title: Regional alignment
claims.effect: Two new substantive security or economic agreements favorable to Iran, sustained for 180 days
claims.falsifier: Defense integration against Iran increases with no comparable accommodation.
claims.support: Durable favorable security and economic arrangements
claims.alternative: Hedging can produce both accommodation and balancing; count both.
claims.attribution: Report-derived hypothesis; not a verified direct quotation from Pape.

claims.title: Nuclear trajectory
claims.statement: Attacks increase long-run nuclear reconstitution incentives.
claims.geography: Iranian nuclear policy and verified facilities
claims.effect: Verified rebuilding plus independently documented policy hardening within 24 months
claims.falsifier: Verified capacity reduction and cooperative inspection sustained for 12 months.
claims.alternative: Inspection gaps are uncertainty; technical capacity and political intent are separate.
claims.attribution: Report-derived hypothesis; not a verified direct quotation from Pape.
claims.plain: Attacks give Iran a stronger long-term reason to rebuild its nuclear program.

claims.title: Net strategic power
claims.geography: Iran relative to its pre-campaign position
claims.effect: Improvement across military regeneration, real trade and durable diplomatic influence over 24 months
claims.falsifier: Deterioration in at least two dimensions sustained for 12 months.
claims.support: Broad improvement in resilience and bargaining outcomes
claims.alternative: Survival and disruption alone do not show an increase in net power.
claims.attribution: Report-derived hypothesis; not a verified direct quotation from Pape.

assessments.rationale: No preregistered campaign objectives and matched outcomes have yet been assembled. Regime survival cannot resolve this claim. Retrospective, provisional analyst judgment using publications dated before the cutoff; no archived as-of snapshot or human approval.

Limited support: the EIA series shows a substantial decline in estimated oil passage. Attribution and persistence under countermeasures remain unverified, so the evidence does not warrant moderate or stronger support. Retrospective, provisional analyst judgment using publications dated before the cutoff; no archived as-of snapshot or human approval.

No reviewed documentary chain connects maritime pressure to a concession sustained for 180 days. Sanctions show costs, not the absence of all concessions. Insufficient evidence. Retrospective, provisional analyst judgment using publications dated before the cutoff; no archived as-of snapshot or human approval.

Slight challenge: the US security guarantee for Qatar is consistent with external balancing. One state and one agreement cannot establish the regional trend; accommodation may coexist. Retrospective, provisional analyst judgment using publications dated before the cutoff; no archived as-of snapshot or human approval.

Inspection gaps establish uncertainty, not incentives or weaponization. Verified rebuilding and a separate policy-intent measure are still required. Retrospective, provisional analyst judgment using publications dated before the cutoff; no archived as-of snapshot or human approval.

Limited challenge: renewed EU sanctions and the IMF adverse growth assessment show diplomatic and economic costs. Military regeneration and durable influence are not measured, so a stronger judgment is not warranted. Retrospective, provisional analyst judgment using publications dated before the cutoff; no archived as-of snapshot or human approval.

evidence.title: Hormuz oil flows: published quarterly estimates
evidence.excerpt: Total oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz | 20.9 | 21.0 | 21.3 | 21.6 | 14.9 | 4.9
evidence.rationale: Lower estimated flow is consistent with disruption. It does not identify the cause or prove retained capability under countermeasures.
evidence.confounders: Demand, supply cuts, rerouting, tracking gaps.
evidence.missingness: No provider coverage denominator or uncertainty interval supplied.
evidence.license: EIA published table; upstream commercial data not redistributed.

evidence.title: IAEA reports a verification gap after the June 2025 attacks
evidence.excerpt: Consequently, the Agency stopped conducting verification activities in Iran.
evidence.rationale: Historical loss of access limits inference. This does not establish weaponization or increased incentives.
evidence.missingness: Not a statement about current inspection access.
evidence.license: Short excerpt with attribution; original document linked.
evidence.effect: Verification access unavailable at reported facilities except Bushehr

evidence.title: EU reimposes nuclear-related sanctions
evidence.excerpt: the Council agreed to reimpose a number of restrictive measures
evidence.rationale: Sanctions are a diplomatic and economic cost. They challenge an unqualified rise in power but do not resolve whether maritime coercion secured some other concession.
evidence.confounders: Nuclear compliance dispute; not necessarily a response to maritime pressure.
evidence.missingness: Later outcomes and persistence require review.
evidence.license: Short excerpt with attribution; original linked.

evidence.title: United States guarantees Qatar against external attack
evidence.excerpt: guarantee the security and territorial integrity of the State of Qatar against external attack
evidence.rationale: A formal US security commitment is consistent with continued external balancing, but is not evidence that Qatar ceased accommodating Iran.
evidence.confounders: The order addresses external attack generally. Its adoption cannot be attributed solely to Iran; threats from Israel are an alternative context.
evidence.missingness: Later outcomes and persistence require review.
evidence.license: Short excerpt with attribution; original linked.

evidence.title: IMF revises Iranian growth downward amid conflict
evidence.excerpt: Growth in Iran in 2026 is revised downward
evidence.rationale: An adverse economic outlook challenges the economic dimension of rising strategic power. A forecast is not a realized GDP result.
evidence.confounders: Conflict, blockade and sanctions overlap; diplomatic and military dimensions remain incomplete.
evidence.missingness: Later outcomes and persistence require review.
evidence.license: Short excerpt with attribution; original linked.

series.name: Oil through the Strait of Hormuz
series.scope: Crude oil and condensate plus petroleum products moving through the strait. LNG is reported separately and is not in the total.
series.note: Source table: EIA analysis based on Vortexa tanker-tracking data. EIA states that AIS data for Hormuz have been especially unreliable since the end of February 2026 and that 2026 figures are revised frequently.

audit.action: Created draft claim tests and provisional November 12 baseline assessments. Five source records; no human approval.
Added per-claim directions to E003: H3 uncertainty only, H6 potential challenge. The record-level direction is kept for compatibility. No level changed.
Added plain-language summaries for H1 and H5 (formal statements unchanged) and reworded coverage-gap descriptions. No level changed.

Added the EIA crude, products and LNG breakdown to the Hormuz series (from E001, Table 4), an AIS reliability note, and a display-only gap entry for economic context. No level, evidence direction or statement changed.

gaps.name: AIS transit coverage
gaps.detail: Daily IMF PortWatch ship counts are shown but not scored. The total number of ships is not known, and AIS misses ships with transponders switched off. EIA states that Hormuz AIS data have been especially unreliable since the end of February 2026.

gaps.name: War-risk insurance
gaps.detail: No licensed insurance-price data. Missing prices are not estimated.

gaps.name: Nuclear verification
gaps.detail: A September 2025 IAEA report is available. Current inspector access and nuclear material records need review.

gaps.name: Diplomatic concessions
gaps.detail: No lasting concession credited to Iranian pressure has been entered. No record does not mean no concession.

gaps.name: Regional / net power
gaps.detail: Treaty, trade, budget and military-rebuilding data still need to be collected and checked.

gaps.name: Iran economy and oil price
gaps.detail: Brent price, the open-market rial rate and annual inflation are shown as context, not scored. The rial rate comes from an unofficial market-data site. Annual inflation is published with a delay of months.
